subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Modern IQ tests (like the Wechsler scales) largely use 'deviation IQ' rather than the classic ratio formula (MA/CA×100) mainly because:

options.option_text: The ratio formula becomes unreliable/meaningless for adults, whose mental age plateaus while chronological age keeps rising
Deviation IQ is easier to calculate mentally without any statistics
The ratio formula works better for adults than for children
Deviation IQ requires no standardised sample at all

explanation: Ratio IQ breaks down for adults since mental age growth plateaus while chronological age keeps increasing. Deviation IQ compares scores to the statistical distribution of same-age peers instead.

subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A diagnosis of intellectual disability requires deficits in both intellectual functioning (low IQ) AND:

options.option_text: Adaptive behaviour (practical, social and conceptual life skills)

explanation: Modern diagnostic criteria require both below-average intellectual functioning AND deficits in adaptive behaviour.
